    StartersLibrary book cheese stacksRosemary lavash crisps stacked with sharp cheddar and thin apple slicesHow to make it2 lavash breads2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil1 bunch rosemary200g vintage cheddar2 applesCut the lavash into neat rectangles, brush with oil and sprinkle with chopped rosemary.Bake at 180°C until crisp, then cool.Stack with slices of cheddar and thin apple slices like a little pile of books.MainsMatilda's pancakesButtermilk pancakes stacked with warm blueberries, butter and maple syrupHow to make it300g plain flour2 tsp baking powder2 tbsp caster sugar500ml buttermilk2 eggs80g butter250g blueberriesmaple syrup, to serveWhisk the flour, baking powder, sugar, buttermilk and eggs.Rest the batter.Cook ladlefuls in butter until bubbles set, then flip.Warm the blueberries in a pan.Stack high with butter, maple syrup and the blueberries.Harry Wormwood's car yard chilli dogsHarry Wormwood's dodgy used car yardHow to make itAs written, serves 4Griddled franks in toasted buns, smothered in beef chilli and cheddar with jammy onions and mustard, a deal even Harry couldn't fiddle.Cook 2 sliced onions in 30g butter for 25 minutes until jammy.Brown 300g beef mince with 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp mild chilli powder and 200g passata and simmer 15 minutes.Simmer 8 franks 5 minutes, then sear on a griddle.Toast 8 hot dog buns.Fill each with a frank, chilli, onions, grated cheddar from 100g and a stripe of mustard.SweetsBruce Bogtrotter's chocolate cakeRich chocolate buttermilk cake covered in thick chocolate frostingHow to make it300g dark chocolate300g butter3 eggs250g caster sugar250ml buttermilk200g plain flour40g cocoa1 tsp bicarb soda150g icing sugarMelt part of the chocolate with part of the butter. Whisk in the eggs, sugar and buttermilk, then fold in the flour, cocoa and bicarb.Bake at 170°C.Cool the cake.Beat melted chocolate with the remaining butter and icing sugar to make the frosting, and cover the cake.Miss Honey's cottage sconesWarm milk scones with strawberry jam and whipped creamHow to make it60g cold butter350g self-raising flour250ml full cream milk1 jar strawberry jam300ml thickened creamRub the butter into the flour.Mix in the milk lightly with a knife, pat out, cut into rounds and pack close on a tray.Bake at 220°C.Whip the cream and serve the scones warm with jam and cream.DrinksTrunchbull's newt-free watermelon coolerWatermelon, lime and mint blended and strained, topped with sparkling waterHow to make it1kg seedless watermelon2 limes1 bunch mint1 tbsp honey500ml sparkling waterice, to serveCut the watermelon flesh into chunks.Blend with the lime juice and mint until smooth.Strain into a jug, pressing on the pulp. Add honey if the melon is not very sweet.Top with sparkling water and plenty of ice. Pour into four glasses with mint sprigs.
